rationale: The ticket's original UM-QODER premise ("scopeId is a write-never dead field, delete to restore upstream") is falsified and, on inspection, UNDER-stated: the field is not merely read in 6 places across 2 files — it has 3 writers and 9 live code readers across 5 data-tool packages, one of which (tool-trigger-eval) is a HARD fail-closed dependency (`if (exec.scopeId === undefined) return not_configured` then passes `scopeId: exec.scopeId` into `EvalRunnerService.runBatch` which itself throws 'explicit scopeId required'). `ToolExecutionInput.scopeId` / `AgentOptions.scopeId` are the session-bound carrier that threads GA-GT1 Phase-5b per-tenant linker isolation end-to-end (the getEnrichedLinker root-check that closes the #19/#22 cross-tenant leak). Retiring the field is a product-capability regression, not a cleanup. Keep-with-waiver is cheap and low-risk: the ONLY cost is 2 doc type-equiv blocks (tools.md:179, core.md:195) that must be edited to include the additive `scopeId?: string` field so verify-type-equiv turns GREEN — i.e. document the fork field rather than suppress it. Note the mechanism is NOT an upstream-sync.json waiver (verify-type-equiv.ts does not read upstream-sync waivers; that array only holds UM-MERGE-INTEGRITY keep-fork/drop-fork path decisions). The "keep-with-waiver" label from the ticket really means: adopt-the-doc-blocks-to-source + type-equiv manifest already maps both symbols, so the 2 DRIFT clear with a documentation edit and no source change. This contradicts the 2026-09-15 'restore upstream for additive violations' principle only superficially — that principle targets write-never dead fields (costs), whereas scopeId is a live, load-bearing seam.

retire.tenantLeakRegressionRisk: HIGH / product-capability regression. exec.scopeId is the carrier that threads GA-GT1 Phase-5b per-tenant isolation: getEnrichedLinker/probeRelationGraph/searchSchema use it as the per-scope cache key WITH a root-check that closes the cross-tenant linker-reuse leak explicitly labeled #19 (and carry-forward #22) in tool-retrieve/tool-search-data-sources/tool-search-schema comments. Today the field is dormant (no prod caller sets AgentOptions.scopeId → undefined → ACTIVE_SENTINEL), but it is the DESIGNED activation seam for 5d eval/CLI per-scope isolation. Deleting it forces per-tenant isolation to be re-plumbed through a different seam (map.md GA-GT1 Phase-5b lists this as the sanctioned mechanism), and removes tool-trigger-eval's fail-closed scope guard — a scoped eval could silently run against the wrong/global scope. This is the exact '撤 per-tenant linker 隔离' regression the 2026-09-11 resync flagged.
